text: Write a Rust function that parses a line of NMEA 0183 GPGGA text into latitude, longitude and fix quality, returning a Result. Include two unit tests.
Write a bash script that finds every file under a directory larger than 1 GB that has not been modified in 30 days and prints its size and path, sorted by size.
In C, implement a ring buffer of bytes with push, pop and a function that reports free space. Keep it single-threaded and explain the full/empty rule you chose.
Write a SQL query against tables orders(id, customer_id, total, created_at) and customers(id, name, region) that returns the top three customers by total spend in each region for 2025.
Write a JavaScript function debounce(fn, ms) and show how to use it on a search box input event. Then explain the difference between debounce and throttle.
Write a Python script that reads a CSV of GPS points (time, lat, lon), computes the distance between consecutive points with the haversine formula and prints total track length in kilometres.
Write a short story of about 200 words about a lighthouse keeper on Lake Erie who notices a light where no ship should be.
Write a friendly letter from a teacher to the parents of a grade five class, announcing a field trip to a maritime museum and listing what students should bring.
Describe a November storm on the Great Lakes from the point of view of a deckhand on a freighter in 1913.
Write a product description for a waterproof handheld GPS aimed at kayakers. Keep it honest and under 150 words.
Write a poem in four stanzas about sonar mapping the bottom of a cold lake.
Summarize the plot of a heist movie you invent, in the style of a newspaper film review.
Write the opening paragraph of a mystery novel set in a small fishing town in winter.
Write a speech of about 150 words thanking volunteers after a successful search and rescue exercise.
Why does sound travel faster in water than in air, and how does water temperature change the speed of sound?
What is the difference between a magnetometer survey and a side-scan sonar survey when searching for a shipwreck?
How does a mixture-of-experts language model decide which experts to use for a token?
Explain photosynthesis to a ten-year-old in a few sentences.
What causes seiches on large lakes, and how large can they get on Lake Erie?
Give me three tips for keeping a sourdough starter alive while on vacation for two weeks.
What is the capital of Australia, and why was it chosen instead of Sydney or Melbourne?
Compare the trade-offs between RAID 5 and RAID 10 for a small home server.

Truth rule: no placeholder or always-empty responses presented as data. Write short, plain Rust.
1. New file src/track.rs: a struct Fix { t: f64, lat: f64, lon: f64 } and `pub fn speed_knots(a: &Fix, b: &Fix) -> Option<f64>` returning None when b.t <= a.t.
2. `pub fn drop_spikes(fixes: &[Fix], max_knots: f64) -> Vec<Fix>` keeps a fix only if the speed from the last kept fix is at most max_knots.
3. Tests: a straight track at 5 knots keeps every fix; one point 10 km off is dropped; equal timestamps do not panic.
Test command: cargo test track

Write short, plain Rust. The CLI tool in src/main.rs reads a JSON manifest of engines ({"name", "port", "enabled"}) and must refuse to start when two enabled engines share a port.
1. Add `pub fn port_conflicts(engines: &[Engine]) -> Vec<(String, String, u16)>` listing each clashing pair once.
2. main prints each conflict as `CONFLICT <a> <b> <port>` and exits 2 if any exist.
3. Disabled engines never conflict.
4. Tests for: no conflicts, one pair, three engines on one port (three pairs), a disabled engine on a used port.
Test command: cargo test port_conflicts

Write short, plain Rust. Implement `pub fn parse_duration(s: &str) -> Result<std::time::Duration, String>` accepting forms like 90s, 15m, 2h, 1h30m and a bare integer meaning seconds. Reject empty input, negative numbers, unknown units and overflow with a clear error message. Add tests for every accepted form and every rejection. Test command: cargo test parse_duration

Truth rule: report failures, never hide them. Write a Rust function `pub fn checksum_ok(line: &str) -> bool` for NMEA sentences: the checksum is the XOR of every byte between '$' and '*', written as two hex digits after '*'. Lines without '*' or with non-hex digits are false. Add tests with one valid GPGGA sentence, one with a wrong checksum, one without a star and one with lower-case hex. Test command: cargo test checksum

Write short, plain Rust. Add an LRU cache `pub struct Lru<K, V>` with `new(capacity)`, `get(&mut self, &K) -> Option<&V>` (marks as used), `put(K, V) -> Option<(K, V)>` (returns the evicted entry) and `len()`. Capacity 0 stores nothing. Use only std. Tests: eviction order, get refreshes recency, put of an existing key updates the value without evicting. Test command: cargo test lru

Write short, plain Rust for a status endpoint. `pub fn health_json(db_age_seconds: u64, max_age: u64) -> serde_json::Value` returns {"ok": bool, "db_age_seconds": n, "stale": bool} where stale is true when the age exceeds max_age and ok is false when stale. Do not return ok=true for a stale database. Tests for fresh, exactly at the limit, and stale. Test command: cargo test health_json

Write short, plain Rust. Implement `pub fn histogram(values: &[f64], bins: usize, lo: f64, hi: f64) -> Vec<u64>`: values below lo go to bin 0, at or above hi to the last bin, NaN values are skipped and counted separately by a second function `pub fn count_nan(values: &[f64]) -> usize`. bins == 0 returns an empty vector. Tests for each edge. Test command: cargo test histogram

Write short, plain Rust. A log line looks like `2026-11-08T06:57:45Z level=warn node=c2 msg="fan at 80%"`. Write `pub fn parse_line(s: &str) -> Option<LogLine>` returning the timestamp string, level, node and the unquoted msg. Missing fields give None; quoted values may contain spaces and escaped quotes. Tests: a full line, a line missing node, a msg with an escaped quote. Test command: cargo test parse_line
